evidence: All survivors immediately construct standard 2-SAT implication graphs: 'Build implication graph for 2-SAT' (qwen3-coder), 'N = 2 * n ... na = la ^ 1; g[na].append(lb)' (gpt-oss-120b), 'nodes: 0..n-1 for x_i, n..2n-1 for ~x_i' (deepseek-v4-flash).
affordance_in_statement: Every rule names exactly two switch-conditions. A rule passes when at least one of its two conditions is met. A condition consists of a switch identifier and the required polarity (either positive for ON, or negative for OFF) that satisfies it.
removal_suggestion: Embed the 2-SAT requirement inside a higher-level domain scenario (e.g., intervals/scheduling, path selection, or mutual exclusion between paired entities) rather than explicitly phrasing the conditions as raw boolean OR-clauses with positive/negative signed literal indices.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: Correctly identified 2-SAT but suffered a logic/implementation bug in the SCC truth assignment phase (topological ordering resolution), resulting in WRONG_ANSWER.

recommended_edit: Reformulate the switch constraints into a contextual setting such as overlapping operational time slots or sensor dependency pairs where the underlying 2-SAT relation must be deduced rather than explicitly handed as boolean OR clauses with signed literal notation.
regression_risk: glm-5 failed purely on SCC implementation details; disguising the problem will not fix its implementation bug and will keep it defeated.
